correctness.rationale: The single-spin transition probability is the squared off-diagonal entry of cos(ωt)I−i sin(ωt)(Ωσx+Δσz)/ω and is the same in both directions, even with nonzero Δ. Product evolution and odd N give the stated binomial tail; summing exponential weights over periods gives (1). For N odd the first admissible mass contributes sqrt(2/(πN)) sqrt(p/(1−p)) [4p(1−p)]^(N/2); the ratios give the geometric multiplier (1−p)/(1−2p), uniformly on compact subcritical intervals. The local quadratic coefficient in I(a sin²θ) is (1−2a)/(2(1−a)), so Gaussian integration yields exactly the prefactor in the Finding. Away from the phase maximum, the entropy Chernoff bound is exponentially smaller. At a_N=1/2+ξ/√N the standardized threshold after phase rescaling tends to u²−2ξ. For an explicit dominating bound use √N(1/2−p)=a_N√N sin²(s)−ξ ≥ c u²−ξ for s=uN^(−1/4), |s|≤π/2, and apply Hoeffding outside a bounded u-region. The weights are uniformly bounded and β_N tends to β_c, proving the full profile. Fubini gives F(0)=2E[(Z_+)^(1/2)], equal to the displayed Gamma constant. In the fixed supercritical regime, the binomial LLN selects the indicated phase interval and bounded convergence gives the quoted weight. The contrast statement is event-indexed, not a law in physical time. Replay: RESULT.md (1)–(2), lines 82–150. The supporting incomplete-beta quadratures are finite diagnostics, read but not executed.
